svg.title: Tengu-Cluster vs Hermes Agent vs PI/Cowork — architecture comparison, April 2026
svg.desc: Three-column comparison across architecture stack, memory model, skills (incl. self-adjustment), tools, routing, five trading-runtime axes added 2026-10-02, A2A interop added 2026-10-10 (typed results + decision loops, long-running runtime, money safety, research on history, engine parity), and four deltas landed on 2026-04-26 (per-example vectors, TUI debug panel, durable user-message persistence, registry recall). Tengu facts refreshed 2026-09-18, 2026-10-02, 2026-10-08 (lineage + forward evidence, sealed strategy rankings, source evidence, counts, skill scanner) and 2026-10-09 (Tengu Studio surface, tool count); Hermes and PI cells on the new axes state only what the snapshot establishes, else "not covered by this snapshot"; the "landed today" boxes are historical.

Tengu is doctrinally sharp (LLM=heart · Open Brain / Karpathy LLM Wiki=brain · tools=hands) but light on agent-layer features —
Hermes wins on breadth (platforms, scheduler, self-improving skills, multi-tenant); PI/Cowork wins on UX (artifacts, computer-use, MCP marketplace).
Since 2026-09 Tengu adds a trading runtime: typed observations + Jev loops, in-tool risk gate + paper ledger, history-first backtests, engine parity, lineage + evidence, sealed rankings.
